description: Service Level Objectives, control-plane, queue, runner and telemetry health from agentsfleetd. Panels 20-25 are the SLO view; everything below panel 4 is the operator view.

panels.description: Service Level Indicator (SLI). Good events: admissions the queue accepted (`appended`) or recognised as an idempotent repeat (`replayed`). Valid events exclude `over_budget`, which is the deployment refusing work on purpose rather than failing at it. Target 99% — a starting threshold, not a measured objective; see docs/architecture/observability.md §Service Level Objectives. Reads 100% when nothing has been admitted, because nothing has failed.
panels.title: SLO · Admission availability

panels.description: SLI. Good events: runs a runner finished with a result (`processed`). Valid events: every finished run — the outcome set is closed at `processed` and `fleet_error`, and a failure moves both this family and agentsfleet_runner_failures_total, so the two agree by construction. Target 95% — a starting threshold. Reads 100% on an idle window.
panels.title: SLO · Runner success rate

panels.description: SLI. The fraction of samples where the oldest unconfirmed admission is younger than the replay floor. The floor is derived from source at apply time (MIN_AGE + INTERVAL in rustd/crates/afd_runner/src/sweep/replay.rs), never typed here: a row younger than MIN_AGE is deliberately left for its own producer, and one older than that should be gone within one sweeper pass. Past the floor means the sweeper is not keeping up. Target 99%.
panels.title: SLO · Work picked up inside the replay floor

panels.description: Seconds since the most overdue runner was last heard from. The family reports a Unix epoch (rustd/crates/afd_observability/src/runner.rs — last_seen_ms / MILLIS_PER_SECOND), so every reader subtracts it from evaluation time; plotting it raw renders tens of thousands of years. Red at the source-derived offline threshold, which is what the runner-silent rule compares against. The aggregation is min-by-runner, not a bare max: the per-runner table is in-process and never evicted, so a runner that heartbeats to one daemon replica leaves a frozen reading on every other replica. Live proof at authoring — runner 019fec54 read 9 s on the replica serving it and 1178 s on its sibling. The freshest observation is the one that is true, because any replica hearing from a runner proves the runner is alive.
panels.title: Worst runner heartbeat age

panels.description:
Service Level Indicator. The one an operator actually wants: a fleet that was asked for was actually started. Good events are fresh lease grants (agentsfleet_fleet_runs_started_total{kind="fresh"}); valid events are admissions the queue accepted. `reclaimed` grants are excluded from the numerator on purpose — a reclaim restarts work that was already admitted and counted once, so counting it again would let a flapping runner push this above 1.

UNPROVEN, and for a different reason than the burn panels: both halves of this ratio come from families newer than the deployed daemon, so there are zero series today. This reads 1 until the next deploy, and the first number worth reading is the one after it.

This indicator was declared impossible on this dashboard until the run-start counter shipped. The denominator was always there.

targets.expr: (1 - (((sum(increase(agentsfleet_admissions_total{outcome="appended"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) - (sum(increase(agentsfleet_fleet_runs_started_total{kind="fresh"}[$__range])) or vector(0))) / clamp_min((sum(increase(agentsfleet_admissions_total{outcome="appended"}[$__range])) or vector(0)), 1))) or vector(1)

panels.title: SLO · Admitted fleets that started

panels.description: Fleets by lifecycle status, one tile each, from a snapshot the census sweeper refreshes every thirty seconds. The five statuses are a closed set, and an absent status publishes zero rather than nothing — a status missing from this row would mean the sweeper failed, not that no fleet holds it. A failed count withdraws every cell at once, so a row that goes blank is a broken sweeper and a row of zeros is an empty deployment. Reads zero until a daemon carrying the family is deployed.
panels.title: Fleets by status

panels.description: Runs begun per second, split by how they came to start. `fresh` is a first grant; `reclaimed` is a lease taken back from a runner that stopped renewing. One family split by cause rather than two families, so a plain sum stays the count of runs begun. A reclaimed line climbing while fresh stays flat is a fleet whose runners are dying and being replaced, which reads as healthy throughput on any panel that sums the two.
panels.title: Runs started by kind

panels.description: UNPROVEN — this deployment has served tens of events, not weeks of them. At the time this panel shipped the whole history was 14 admissions and 10 runner executions, so the burn rate below is arithmetic over a sample too small to set an objective from. Read the shape, not the number, until the windows are full. Google Site Reliability Engineering workbook shape: burn rate is the error ratio divided by the error budget (1 - target). Two windows per severity — the long window makes the budget claim and the short window resets it, so a burn that has already stopped does not keep paging. Page when 1h AND 5m both exceed 14.4 (2% of a 30-day budget in an hour); open a ticket when 6h AND 30m both exceed 6.
panels.title: Error budget burn — admission availability (unproven)

panels.description: UNPROVEN — this deployment has served tens of events, not weeks of them. At the time this panel shipped the whole history was 14 admissions and 10 runner executions, so the burn rate below is arithmetic over a sample too small to set an objective from. Read the shape, not the number, until the windows are full. Same multiwindow, multi-burn-rate shape against the 95% runner-success target, so the budget divisor is 0.05. A sustained 1h burn above 14.4 spends 2% of a 30-day budget in an hour.
panels.title: Error budget burn — runner success (unproven)
Runner heartbeat age
panels.description: Seconds since each runner's last heartbeat. Subtracted from evaluation time because the family carries an epoch, not an age — the same repair panel 23 and the runner-silent rule carry. The aggregation is min-by-runner, not a bare max: the per-runner table is in-process and never evicted, so a runner that heartbeats to one daemon replica leaves a frozen reading on every other replica. Live proof at authoring — runner 019fec54 read 9 s on the replica serving it and 1178 s on its sibling. The freshest observation is the one that is true, because any replica hearing from a runner proves the runner is alive.

panels.title: Telemetry loss at the source
panels.description: Whether this dashboard can see. Discarded OpenTelemetry entries counted by the exporter itself, by signal and reason, plus attribute omissions. The queue-depth series this panel once carried is gone on purpose: agentsfleet_otlp_queue_depth has no producer — the software development kit owns the export queue and exposes no depth — and a target for it drew an empty line that read as health. The UNPRODUCED ledger in rustd/crates/afd_observability/src/metrics/produced.rs names it, and names this counter as the surviving local-loss signal. An empty panel here means nothing was dropped.

What is being retried rather than failing outright. Admission replays are the sweeper re-appending rows the queue never took; repair dispatch retries are verifier dispatch attempts awaiting another pass; hub reconnects are pub/sub redials, and a spike there means datastore instability. Each of these is work the system is absorbing — a rising line is the warning before the failure, not the failure.
panels.title: Retry and replay pressure

panels.description: In-flight requests read against api_max_in_flight_requests; in-flight streams against the stream cap; ready-fleet depth is a readiness backlog and is not summable across replicas, so it is taken as a maximum; admission backlog is admitted rows the queue has not confirmed, and a rising line there is a queue refusing appends.
panels.title: Saturation — how full, against what

panels.description: Age of the oldest unconfirmed admission and of the oldest due verifier intent, against the source-derived replay floor drawn as a flat line. Depth says how much is waiting; age says how long the oldest of it has waited, and only the second one tells you a sweeper has stopped.
panels.title: Backlog age — the oldest thing still waiting

panels.description: Generated from the `category` column of docs/metrics.census.tsv, not hand-listed, so a family added to the census appears here without anyone remembering to add it. Every tile carries `or vector(0)`: a counter that has never incremented publishes NO series, and a family absent from this panel would be indistinguishable from one that was never wired up. Green zero means it has genuinely never happened. Eighteen error families, one tile each, red above zero. This is the panel that answers 'is anything failing' without knowing in advance what could fail.
panels.title: Every error family — including the silent ones

panels.description: Generated from the `category` column of docs/metrics.census.tsv, not hand-listed, so a family added to the census appears here without anyone remembering to add it. Every tile carries `or vector(0)`: a counter that has never incremented publishes NO series, and a family absent from this panel would be indistinguishable from one that was never wired up. Green zero means it has genuinely never happened. Twelve saturation families read as their current value. Depth without age is half a story; panel 28 carries the ages.
panels.title: Every saturation family — how full, everywhere

panels.description: Generated from the `category` column of docs/metrics.census.tsv, not hand-listed, so a family added to the census appears here without anyone remembering to add it. Every tile carries `or vector(0)`: a counter that has never incremented publishes NO series, and a family absent from this panel would be indistinguishable from one that was never wired up. Green zero means it has genuinely never happened. Nine health families. These are not about the workload: they are about whether the machinery reporting on the workload is itself intact.
panels.title: Every health family — is the plumbing working

panels.description: Generated from the `category` column of docs/metrics.census.tsv, not hand-listed, so a family added to the census appears here without anyone remembering to add it. Every tile carries `or vector(0)`: a counter that has never incremented publishes NO series, and a family absent from this panel would be indistinguishable from one that was never wired up. Green zero means it has genuinely never happened. Traffic and latency families as counts over the window — the denominator that makes an error count mean something. A spike in errors beside a spike in traffic is a different incident from a spike in errors alone.
panels.title: Traffic and latency volume

panels.description: Declared metric gaps and the shared-tenant warning.

options.content:
### What this dashboard cannot show you, and why

Eleven families are declared in `docs/metrics.census.tsv` and have **no producer** in this build.
The ledger is `rustd/crates/afd_observability/src/metrics/produced.rs`; each line below quotes its
reason. A gap is on this screen rather than in a document because the families an operator reaches
for first at 3am are two of the ones that are missing.

| Family | Why nothing feeds it |
|---|---|
| `agentsfleet.telemetry.samples_dropped` | the ring it counted belongs to the daemon being replaced |
| `agentsfleet_otlp_queue_depth` | the software development kit owns the export queue and exposes no depth |
| `agentsfleet_repair_production_to_queue_seconds` | the repair-result ingress has no Rust home yet |
| `agentsfleet_repair_queue_to_completion_seconds` | the repair-result ingress has no Rust home yet |
| `agentsfleet_repair_provider_results_total` | the repair-result ingress has no Rust home yet |
| `agentsfleet_repair_correlations_total` | the repair-result ingress has no Rust home yet |
| `agentsfleet_repair_verification_intents_created_total` | the repair-result ingress has no Rust home yet |
| `agentsfleet_account_teardown_unregister_failures_total` | account teardown is declared unported |
| `agentsfleet_http_trace_suppressed_total` | every matched request is traced, so nothing is suppressed to count |
| `agentsfleet_library_cache_outcome_total` | the revision-keyed response cache is a declared non-port |
| `agentsfleet_library_pool_result_total` | the acquire happens inside the store, where the read path cannot see how it ended |

**End-to-end fleet availability is no longer impossible — it is panel 34.** The run-start counter
now supplies the numerator this dashboard used to say did not exist: `agentsfleet_fleet_runs_started_total{kind}`,
incremented at the one lease grant point. The denominator was always here as
`agentsfleet_admissions_total{outcome="appended"}`. It reads 1 until a daemon carrying those
families is deployed. The trigger counter this dashboard used to cite as the missing denominator
was retired alongside it: declared and incremented nowhere, it left the census rather than gaining
a producer.

**Repair latency is still impossible.** Both repair histograms sit in the ledger above behind an
ingress with no Rust home, so there is no threshold waiting to be tuned: the family has no
producer at all.

There is also **no HTTP request-duration histogram anywhere in the census**, so the most standard
Service Level Indicator of all — API latency — cannot be drawn here at any target.

### This dashboard is development-only by accident, not by design

Development and production resolve to the **same Grafana stack, the same namespace, the same
Prometheus datasource and the same ingest credential**, and no series carries a
`deployment.environment` attribute — the daemon's resource is service name, namespace, version and
an optional instance identifier, and nothing else. Today every series here is development because
the production Fly application runs zero machines. **The day production deploys, every panel above
silently sums both environments and no query can separate them.** Emitting
`deployment.environment` is the named blocker on that deploy.

panels.title: Declared gaps · what this dashboard cannot show
